critical_code_review_comments: Fix addresses the reported bug at the correct layer: replacing balance-delta polling (which is inherently ambiguous when trades overlap) with DOM-row matching against a FIFO of armed trades is the right architectural choice.
Executor still calls the deprecated _scheduleOutcomeResolution stub — safe (no-op) but consider removing the call site entirely in a future cleanup to avoid dead-code confusion.

Note: static-source tests cannot detect runtime edge cases (e.g. DOM selector drift on pocketoption.com, race between MutationObserver and interval scan, duplicate row matching under identical asset/direction/amount trades). A manual smoke test with two overlapping 60s trades on the same asset is still recommended once the extension is loaded in a browser.

context_for_next_testing_agent: iter136 covers Tampermonkey userscript trade-outcome detection rewrite. Tests are pure static/source assertions (no live pocketoption.com interaction possible in sandbox). Regression order used: iter131,133,134,135,136 — all green. If iter131/133 shared-state timing issue resurfaces, that ordering avoids the collision (iter131 uses user_id 'riskguard_pytest', iter133 uses 'default' and wipes at end).
rca of the issue: Original bug: balance-delta detection (preBalance vs postBalance after expirySeconds) was inherently unreliable because (a) only one armed trade tracked at a time (this.armed single slot), and (b) if a new trade's stake was deducted before the previous trade's payout landed, the delta became ambiguous (net negative/positive of two trades). Fix: (1) armedQueue FIFO holds all pending trades; (2) MutationObserver + periodic scan of the deals table parses new rows and matches them to the OLDEST armed trade with matching (asset, direction, amount within ~5c); (3) balance polling entirely removed; (4) executor's redundant balance-based resolver reduced to a documented no-op stub.
